faqs.q: What does a digital marketing agency for the pharmaceutical industry do?
faqs.a: It helps pharmacies and consumer health brands reach people searching for medicines, stores and wellness products, while staying within advertising law. That covers Google Ads, Google Maps, SEO, social media and WhatsApp, with every enquiry tracked to an order or store visit.

faqs.q: Can pharmaceutical companies advertise medicines online in India?
faqs.a: Only within strict limits. Indian law restricts advertising prescription medicines to the public and bans claims that a product cures listed diseases. Pharma companies can share approved health education, and promote over-the-counter and wellness products with accurate, non-misleading claims.

Yes, with care. Google restricts medicine-related advertising, and online pharmacies usually need certification before running ads. Store-focused campaigns for location, opening hours, delivery and services are simpler to approve, and prescription medicines should never feature in ad copy.

faqs.q: How can a pharmacy compete with online pharmacy apps?
faqs.a: Compete on what apps can’t offer: speed, trust and a pharmacist nearby. Promote same-day delivery, quick WhatsApp ordering and pharmacist advice. Refill reminders keep regular customers loyal, so they reorder from your store instead of comparing app discounts every month.

faqs.q: Which keywords should pharmacies target on Google?
faqs.a: Target searches with clear local intent: “pharmacy near me,” “24-hour chemist near me,” “medical store in [locality],” “medicine home delivery in [city]” and “[product] available near me.” Avoid prescription drug names in paid ads, and use health topics for educational content instead.

faqs.q: Does a pharmacy need a website, or is Google Maps enough?
faqs.a: Google Maps brings the quickest local visibility, but a website adds trust and reach. It lets customers check services, delivery areas and timings, and place orders on WhatsApp. Together, they capture both “near me” searches and people comparing pharmacies before buying.
